title: Acids and Alkalis
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Acids and Alkalis Worksheets (pH Scale, Indicators, Neutralisation)
standard_text: Defining acids and alkalis in terms of neutralisation reactions; the pH scale for measuring acidity/alkalinity; and indicators; reactions of acids with alkalis to produce a salt plus water.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on acids and alkalis: the pH scale, universal indicator and litmus, acids and alkalis at home, neutralisation and naming salts. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Below 7 is acidic, above 7 is alkaline. Acid + alkali → salt + water.
body_html:
How to think about it

The pH scale shows how acidic or alkaline a solution is.

  • pH below 7: acid (lower is stronger). pH 7: neutral. Above 7: alkali (higher is stronger).
  • Universal indicator: red/orange/yellow for acids, green for neutral, blue/purple for alkalis.
  • Neutralisation: acid + alkali → salt + water. Hydrochloric acid makes chlorides, sulfuric acid sulfates, nitric acid nitrates.
Example

pH 13 is?

Far above 7

Answer: a strong alkali

Example

Hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → ?

Chloride salt

Answer: sodium chloride + water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking pH 1 is weakly acidic.
  • Thinking neutral means pH 0.
  • Thinking all acids are dangerous.
